'''Louis Bryant Tuckerman III''' (November 28, 1915 – May 19, 2002) was an American mathematician. He was a member of the team that developed the [[Data Encryption Standard]] (DES).<ref name=bio />

He studied [[topology]] at [[Princeton University|Princeton]], where he invented the [[Tuckerman traverse]] method for revealing all the faces of a [[flexagon]].<ref name=bio />

On March 4, 1971, he discovered the 24th [[Mersenne prime]],<ref>{{cite journal|last=Tuckerman|first=Bryant|title=The 24th Mersenne Prime|journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]]|date=October 1971|volume=68|issue=10|pages=2319–2320|doi=10.1073/pnas.68.10.2319|jstor=61035|pmid=16591945|pmc=389411|bibcode=1971PNAS...68.2319T |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Caldwell|first=Chris|title=Mersenne Primes: History, Theorems and Lists|url=http://primes.utm.edu/mersenne/|access-date=February 21, 2013}}</ref> a [[titanic prime]], with a value of

:<math>2^{19937}-1</math>.
